title: DNA gyrase as the fluoroquinolone enzyme node
dek: Wikipedia DNA gyrase page. QRDR alleles and moxifloxacin/levofloxacin plates already own TB use.
story: DNA gyrase on Wikipedia is the type II topoisomerase that introduces negative supercoils. Fluoroquinolones poison it. Mtb has gyrase (GyrA/GyrB) and does not have the same topoisomerase IV story Gram-negatives do — a glossary distinction that explains why gyrA QRDR is the TB FQ celebrity.
tb-gyr-qrdr and the named FQ plates own alleles and doses. This card is the enzyme in the encyclopedia graph.
Do not pick ciprofloxacin from a gyrase infobox.
deep: QRDR is a short stretch of gyrA/gyrB; the enzyme is larger than the window.
Xpert XDR looks at a subset of FQ-associated changes — cartridge plate.
Mtb's lack of ParC/ParE as a second FQ target is why gyrA mutations matter so much.

visual.caption: GyrA schematic with QRDR marked as a pointer to tb-gyr-qrdr, not as a new catalogue.
